sanskrit: adhīyate 'dhyāpayanti yajante yājayanti ca dadati pratigṛhṇanti ṣaṭsu karmasv avasthitāḥ
english: They study and they teach, they sacrifice and they officiate at sacrifice, they give and they receive — firmly established in the six prescribed duties.

sanskrit: pūjitāḥ saṃvibhaktāś ca mṛdavaḥ satyavādinaḥ brāhmaṇā me svakarmasthā māmakāntaram āviśaḥ
english: Honored and provided for, gentle and truthful in speech — my Brāhmaṇas abide in their own duty: enter into my inmost self.

sanskrit: na yācante prayacchanti satyadharmaviśāradāḥ nādhyāpayanty adhīyante yajante na ca yājakāḥ
english: They do not beg but bestow, skilled in truth and in dharma; they do not teach for hire nor study as pupils, they sacrifice but do not officiate as priests.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇān parirakṣanti saṃgrāmeṣv apalāyinaḥ kṣatriyā me svakarmasthā māmakāntaram āviśaḥ
english: They protect the Brāhmaṇas and never flee from battles — my Kṣatriyas abide in their own duty: enter into my inmost self.

sanskrit: kṛṣigorakṣavāṇijyam upajīvanty amāyayā apramattāḥ kriyāvantaḥ suvratāḥ satyavādinaḥ
english: By farming, cattle-tending, and trade they earn their living without deceit — vigilant, performing their rites, true to their vows, truthful in speech.

sanskrit: saṃvibhāgaṃ damaṃ śaucaṃ sauhṛdaṃ ca vyapāśritāḥ mama vaiśyāḥ svakarmasthā māmakāntaram āviśaḥ
english: Devoted to sharing, self-restraint, purity, and goodwill — my Vaiśyas abide in their own duty: enter into my inmost self.

sanskrit: trīn varṇān anutiṣṭhanti yathāvad anasūyakāḥ mama śūdrāḥ svakarmasthā māmakāntaram āviśaḥ
english: They serve the three higher orders duly and without envy — my Śūdras abide in their own duty: enter into my inmost self.

sanskrit: kṛpaṇānāthavṛddhānāṃ durbalāturayoṣitām saṃvibhaktāsmi sarveṣāṃ māmakāntaram āviśaḥ
english: To the wretched, the helpless, the aged, the weak, the sick, and to women — to all of these I have given a share: enter into my inmost self.

sanskrit: kuladeśādidharmāṇāṃ prathitānāṃ yathāvidhi avyucchettāsmi sarveṣāṃ māmakāntaram āviśaḥ
english: Of the established duties of family and region and the rest, I am one who, as prescribed, lets none of them lapse: enter into my inmost self.

sanskrit: tapasvino me viṣaye pūjitāḥ paripālitāḥ saṃvibhaktāś ca satkṛtya māmakāntaram āviśaḥ
english: The ascetics in my realm are honored and protected, given their share and treated with respect: enter into my inmost self.

sanskrit: nāsaṃvibhajya bhoktāsmi na viśāmi parastriyam svatantro jātu na krīḍe māmakāntaram āviśaḥ
english: I never eat without first sharing, I never approach another man's wife, I never sport as one wholly self-willed: enter into my inmost self.

sanskrit: nābrahmacārī bhikṣāvān bhikṣur vābrahmacārikaḥ anṛtvijaṃ hutaṃ nāsti māmakāntaram āviśaḥ
english: In my realm no mendicant lives uncontinent, no continent man is left to beg; no offering is poured save through a proper priest: enter into my inmost self.

sanskrit: nāvajānāmy ahaṃ vṛddhān na vaidyān na tapasvinaḥ rāṣṭre svapati jāgarmi māmakāntaram āviśaḥ
english: I despise neither the aged nor the learned nor the ascetics; I keep watch while my kingdom sleeps: enter into my inmost self.

sanskrit: vedādhyayanasaṃpannas tapasvī sarvadharmavit svāmī sarvasya rājyasya śrīmān mama purohitaḥ
english: Accomplished in the study of the Veda, an ascetic, knower of all dharma, master of the whole kingdom — such is my illustrious household priest.

sanskrit: dānena divyān abhivāñchāmi lokān; satyenātho brāhmaṇānāṃ ca guptyā śuśrūṣayā cāpi gurūn upaimi; na me bhayaṃ vidyate rākṣasebhyaḥ
english: By giving I long for the celestial worlds; by truth, and by guarding the Brāhmaṇas, and by attendance I draw near to my elders — I have no fear of the Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: na me rāṣṭre vidhavā brahmabandhur; na brāhmaṇaḥ kṛpaṇo nota coraḥ na pārajāyī na ca pāpakarmā; na me bhayaṃ vidyate rākṣasebhyaḥ
english: In my realm there is no widow, no Brāhmaṇa in name only, no Brāhmaṇa fallen to poverty, nor any thief, no adulterer, no doer of evil — I have no fear of the Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: na me śastrair anirbhinnam aṅge dvyaṅgulam antaram dharmārthaṃ yudhyamānasya māmakāntaram āviśaḥ
english: On my body, as I fight for the sake of dharma, there is no span of two fingers' breadth unbroken by weapons: enter into my inmost self.

sanskrit: gobrāhmaṇe ca yajñe ca nityaṃ svastyayanaṃ mama āśāsate janā rāṣṭre māmakāntaram āviśaḥ
english: For cattle and Brāhmaṇas and for sacrifice the people of my realm forever pray my well-being: enter into my inmost self.

sanskrit: rākṣasa uvāca yasmāt sarvāsv avasthāsu dharmam evānvavekṣase tasmāt prāpnuhi kaikeya gṛhān svasti vrajāmy aham
english: The Rākṣasa said: Since in every circumstance you look only to dharma, therefore reach your home in safety, O Kaikeya — and I depart in peace.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ gobrāhmaṇā rakṣyāḥ prajā rakṣyāś ca kekaya na rakṣobhyo bhayaṃ teṣāṃ kuta eva tu mānuṣāt
english: They who guard their cattle and Brāhmaṇas and protect their subjects, O Kekaya, have nothing to fear from the Rākṣasas — how much less from any man?

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ purogamā viprā yeṣāṃ brahmabalaṃ balam priyātithyās tathā dārās te vai svargajito narāḥ
english: Those whose leaders are the learned, whose strength is the strength of brahman, whose wives hold guests dear — those men have surely won heaven.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tasmād dvijātīn rakṣeta te hi rakṣanti rakṣitāḥ āśīr eṣāṃ bhaved rājñāṃ rāṣṭraṃ samyak pravardhate
english: Bhīṣma said: Therefore let the king protect the twice-born, for they, when protected, protect in return; their blessing falls upon kings, and the kingdom flourishes aright.

sanskrit: tasmād rājñā viśeṣeṇa vikarmasthā dvijātayaḥ niyamyāḥ saṃvibhajyāś ca prajānugrahakāraṇāt
english: Therefore the king must especially restrain those twice-born who stray into wrongful acts, and must provide for them, for the welfare of the people.

sanskrit: ya evaṃ vartate rājā paurajānapadeṣv iha anubhūyeha bhadrāṇi prāpnotīndrasalokatām
english: The king who conducts himself thus toward townsfolk and country folk, having enjoyed blessings here, attains to dwelling in the world of Indra.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca vyākhyātā kṣatradharmeṇa vṛttir āpatsu bhārata kathaṃ cid vaiśyadharmeṇa jīved vā brāhmaṇo na vā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The livelihood proper in times of distress has been expounded by way of the Kṣatriya's dharma, O Bhārata; but may a Brāhmaṇa somehow live by the dharma of a Vaiśya, or may he not?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca aśaktaḥ kṣatradharmeṇa vaiśyadharmeṇa vartayet kṛṣigorakṣam āsthāya vyasane vṛttisaṃkṣaye
english: Bhīṣma said: One unable to subsist by the Kṣatriya's dharma may live by the Vaiśya's dharma, taking up farming and cattle-tending in calamity, when his livelihood has failed.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kāni paṇyāni vikrīṇan svargalokān na hīyate brāhmaṇo vaiśyadharmeṇa vartayan bharatarṣabha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Selling which wares does a Brāhmaṇa, living by the Vaiśya's dharma, not fall from the heavenly worlds, O bull of the Bharatas?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca surā lavaṇam ity eva tilān kesariṇaḥ paśūn ṛṣabhān madhu māṃsaṃ ca kṛtānnaṃ ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: Liquor and salt, sesame, lions and other beasts, bulls, honey and flesh, and cooked food, O Yudhiṣṭhira —

sanskrit: sarvāsv avasthāsv etāni brāhmaṇaḥ parivarjayet eteṣāṃ vikrayāt tāta brāhmaṇo narakaṃ vrajet
english: in all conditions a Brāhmaṇa should avoid these; for from selling them, my son, a Brāhmaṇa goes to hell.

sanskrit: ajo 'gnir varuṇo meṣaḥ sūryo 'śvaḥ pṛthivī virāṭ dhenur yajñaś ca somaś ca na vikreyāḥ kathaṃ cana
english: The goat is Agni, the ram is Varuṇa, the horse is Sūrya, the earth is Virāṭ; the milch-cow, the sacrifice, and the Soma — these are never to be sold by any means.

sanskrit: pakvenāmasya nimayaṃ na praśaṃsanti sādhavaḥ nimayet pakvam āmena bhojanārthāya bhārata
english: The good do not commend the barter of raw for cooked; yet one may exchange cooked for raw for the sake of food, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vayaṃ siddham aśiṣyāmo bhavān sādhayatām idam evaṃ samīkṣya nimayan nādharmo 'sti kadā cana
english: "We shall eat what is already cooked; let your honor prepare this raw food" — exchanging with such an understanding, there is never any unrighteousness.

sanskrit: atra te vartayiṣyāmi yathā dharmaḥ purātanaḥ vyavahārapravṛttānāṃ tan nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: On this I shall set forth for you what the ancient dharma was for those engaged in commerce; learn it, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: bhavate 'haṃ dadānīdaṃ bhavān etat prayacchatu rucite vartate dharmo na balāt saṃpravartate
english: "I give this to your honor; let your honor in turn grant that" — dharma proceeds by mutual consent, never by force.

sanskrit: ity evaṃ saṃpravartanta vyavahārāḥ purātanāḥ ṛṣīṇām itareṣāṃ ca sādhu cedam asaṃśayam
english: Thus did the dealings of old proceed, among the seers and among others alike; and this, beyond doubt, is good.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca atha tāta yadā sarvāḥ śastram ādadate prajāḥ vyutkrāmanti svadharmebhyaḥ kṣatrasya kṣīyate balam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: But, father, when all the people take up arms and depart from their own duties, and the strength of the Kṣatriya order wanes —

sanskrit: rājā trātā na loke syāt kiṃ tadā syāt parāyaṇam etan me saṃśayaṃ brūhi vistareṇa pitāmaha
english: when there is no king to be a protector in the world, what then would be the refuge? Resolve this doubt of mine in full, O grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca dānena tapasā yajñair adroheṇa damena ca brāhmaṇapramukhā varṇāḥ kṣemam iccheyur ātmanaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: By giving, by austerity, by sacrifices, by freedom from malice, and by self-restraint, the orders headed by the Brāhmaṇas should seek their own security.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ ye vedabalinas ta utthāya samantataḥ rājño balaṃ vardhayeyur mahendrasyeva devatāḥ
english: Among them, those strong in the Veda, rising up on every side, should increase the king's strength, as the gods increase the strength of great Indra.

sanskrit: rājño hi kṣīyamāṇasya brahmaivāhuḥ parāyaṇam tasmād brahmabalenaiva samuttheyaṃ vijānatā
english: For when a king is failing, they say that brahman alone is his refuge; therefore one who knows should rise up by the power of brahman itself.

sanskrit: yadā tu vijayī rājā kṣemaṃ rāṣṭre 'bhisaṃdadhet tadā varṇā yathādharmam āviśeyuḥ svakarmasu
english: But when a victorious king has secured the kingdom's safety, then let the orders enter again, each according to its dharma, upon their own tasks.

sanskrit: unmaryāde pravṛtte tu dasyubhiḥ saṃkare kṛte sarve varṇā na duṣyeyuḥ śastravanto yudhiṣṭhira
english: But when all bounds are overthrown and confusion is wrought by brigands, then all the orders, though bearing arms, incur no fault, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca atha cet sarvataḥ kṣatraṃ praduṣyed brāhmaṇān prati kas tasya brāhmaṇas trātā ko dharmaḥ kiṃ parāyaṇam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: But if the Kṣatriya order should everywhere turn evil against the Brāhmaṇas, who then is the Brāhmaṇa's protector, what is his dharma, what his refuge?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tapasā brahmacaryeṇa śastreṇa ca balena ca amāyayā māyayā ca niyantavyaṃ tadā bhavet
english: Bhīṣma said: By austerity, by chastity, by the weapon and by force, by honest means and by stratagem, it must then be brought under control.

sanskrit: kṣatrasyābhipravṛddhasya brāhmaṇeṣu viśeṣataḥ brahmaiva saṃniyantṛ syāt kṣatraṃ hi brahmasaṃbhavam
english: When the Kṣatriya power has grown overweening, especially against the Brāhmaṇas, brahman alone should be its restrainer; for the Kṣatriya order springs from brahman.

sanskrit: adbhyo 'gnir brahmataḥ kṣatram aśmano loham utthitam teṣāṃ sarvatragaṃ tejaḥ svāsu yoniṣu śāmyati
english: From water arose fire, from brahman the Kṣatriya, from stone iron; the all-pervading fierce energy of these is quenched in its own source.

sanskrit: yadā chinatty ayo 'śmānam agniś cāpo 'bhipadyate kṣatraṃ ca brāhmaṇaṃ dveṣṭi tadā śāmyanti te trayaḥ
english: When iron cleaves the stone, when fire assails the waters, and when the Kṣatriya hates the Brāhmaṇa — then these three are quelled.

sanskrit: tasmād brahmaṇi śāmyanti kṣatriyāṇāṃ yudhiṣṭhira samudīrṇāny ajeyāni tejāṃsi ca balāni ca
english: Therefore in brahman, O Yudhiṣṭhira, the surging, unconquerable fiery energies and forces of the Kṣatriyas are quelled.

sanskrit: brahmavīrye mṛdūbhūte kṣatravīrye ca durbale duṣṭeṣu sarvavarṇeṣu brāhmaṇān prati sarvaśaḥ
english: When the might of brahman has grown soft and the might of the Kṣatriya weak, and all the orders have turned wholly evil against the Brāhmaṇas —

sanskrit: ye tatra yuddhaṃ kurvanti tyaktvā jīvitam ātmanaḥ brāhmaṇān parirakṣanto dharmam ātmānam eva ca
english: those who then make war, surrendering their own lives, guarding the Brāhmaṇas, and dharma, and their own souls —

sanskrit: manasvino manyumantaḥ puṇyalokā bhavanti te brāhmaṇārthaṃ hi sarveṣāṃ śastragrahaṇam iṣyate
english: those high-minded and wrathful men win the worlds of the meritorious; for the taking up of arms by all is sanctioned for the Brāhmaṇas' sake.

sanskrit: ati sviṣṭasvadhītānāṃ lokān ati tapasvinām anāśakāgnyor viśatāṃ śūrā yānti parāṃ gatim evam evātmanas tyāgān nānyaṃ dharmaṃ vidur janāḥ
english: Beyond the worlds of those who have sacrificed well and studied well, beyond those of ascetics and of those who enter into fasting unto death or into the fire — the heroes go to the highest goal; thus, through the surrender of self, men know no higher dharma.

sanskrit: tebhyo namaś ca bhadraṃ ca ye śarīrāṇi juhvati brahmadviṣo niyacchantas teṣāṃ no 'stu salokatā brahmalokajitaḥ svargyān vīrāṃs tān manur abravīt
english: Homage and benediction to them who offer up their bodies, restraining the haters of brahman; may we share their world. Manu declared those heroes winners of the world of brahman and worthy of heaven.

sanskrit: yathāśvamedhāvabhṛthe snātāḥ pūtā bhavanty uta duṣkṛtaḥ sukṛtaś caiva tathā śastrahatā raṇe
english: As those who have bathed in the final ablution of the horse-sacrifice are purified, so too, both the evildoer and the doer of good, are those slain by the sword in battle.

sanskrit: bhavaty adharmo dharmo hi dharmādharmāv ubhāv api kāraṇād deśakālasya deśakālaḥ sa tādṛśaḥ
english: What is unrighteous becomes righteous; both righteousness and unrighteousness, by reason of place and time — and such is that place and time.

sanskrit: maitrāḥ krūrāṇi kurvanto jayanti svargam uttamam dharmyāḥ pāpāni kurvanto gacchanti paramāṃ gatim
english: The friendly, doing cruel deeds, win the highest heaven; the righteous, doing what seem sinful deeds, reach the supreme goal.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇas triṣu kāleṣu śastraṃ gṛhṇan na duṣyati ātmatrāṇe varṇadoṣe durgasya niyameṣu ca
english: On three occasions a Brāhmaṇa, taking up the weapon, incurs no fault: in defense of his own life, in a confounding of the orders, and amid the constraints of a besieged stronghold.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca abhyutthite dasyubale kṣatrārthe varṇasaṃkare saṃpramūḍheṣu varṇeṣu yady anyo 'bhibhaved balī
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When a host of brigands has risen up, in the cause of the Kṣatriya order, amid a confusion of castes, when the orders are utterly bewildered — if another, a strong man, should prevail,

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo yadi vā vaiśyaḥ śūdro vā rājasattama dasyubhyo 'tha prajā rakṣed daṇḍaṃ dharmeṇa dhārayan
english: a Brāhmaṇa or a Vaiśya or a Śūdra, O best of kings, and he should protect the people from the brigands, wielding the rod of punishment in accordance with dharma —

sanskrit: kāryaṃ kuryān na vā kuryāt saṃvāryo vā bhaven na vā na sma śastraṃ grahītavyam anyatra kṣatrabandhutaḥ
english: should this be done or not done? Should he be restrained or not? Or is the weapon never to be taken up by any save those of Kṣatriya kin?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca apāre yo bhavet pāram aplave yaḥ plavo bhavet śūdro vā yadi vāpy anyaḥ sarvathā mānam arhati
english: Bhīṣma said: Whoever proves a farther shore where there is none, a raft where there is no boat — be he a Śūdra or any other — by all means deserves honor.

sanskrit: yam āśritya narā rājan vartayeyur yathāsukham anāthāḥ pālyamānā vai dasyubhiḥ paripīḍitāḥ
english: He under whose shelter men may live at their ease, O king — men once helpless, now protected, who had been afflicted by brigands —

sanskrit: tam eva pūjayeraṃs te prītyā svam iva bāndhavam mahad dhy abhīkṣṇaṃ kauravya kartā sanmānam arhati
english: him let those men honor with affection as their own kinsman; for one who does great service again and again, O Kaurava, deserves esteem.

sanskrit: kim ukṣṇāvahatā kṛtyaṃ kiṃ dhenvā cāpy adugdhayā vandhyayā bhāryayā ko 'rthaḥ ko 'rtho rājñāpy arakṣatā
english: What use is an ox that bears no burden, what use a cow that yields no milk? What good is a barren wife? And what good is a king who does not protect?

sanskrit: yathā dārumayo hastī yathā carmamayo mṛgaḥ yathā hy anetraḥ śakaṭaḥ pathi kṣetraṃ yathoṣaram
english: As an elephant made of wood, as a deer made of leather, as a cart without a driver, as a barren field beside the road —

sanskrit: evaṃ brahmānadhīyānaṃ rājā yaś ca na rakṣitā na varṣati ca yo meghaḥ sarva ete nirarthakāḥ
english: so a Brāhmaṇa who does not study his Veda, a king who does not protect, and a cloud that does not rain — all these are without purpose.

sanskrit: nityaṃ yas tu sato rakṣed asataś ca nibarhayet sa eva rājā kartavyas tena sarvam idaṃ dhṛtam
english: But he who ever protects the good and strikes down the wicked — he alone should be made king; by him is all this world upheld.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kvasamutthāḥ kathaṃśīlā ṛtvijaḥ syuḥ pitāmaha kathaṃvidhāś ca rājendra tad brūhi vadatāṃ vara
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Of what origin, of what character, and of what kind should the officiating priests be, O grandfather, O lord of kings? Tell me that, O best of speakers.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca pratikarma purācāra ṛtvijāṃ sma vidhīyate ādau chandāṃsi vijñāya dvijānāṃ śrutam eva ca
english: Bhīṣma said: For each rite the ancient usage of the officiating priests is prescribed: first, having ascertained the metres and the sacred learning of the twice-born.

sanskrit: ye tv ekaratayo nityaṃ dhīrā nāpriyavādinaḥ parasparasya suhṛdaḥ saṃmatāḥ samadarśinaḥ
english: Those who are ever single-minded, steadfast, who speak no unkind word, friends to one another, respected, and even-sighted toward all;

sanskrit: yeṣv ānṛśaṃsyaṃ satyaṃ cāpy ahiṃsā tapa ārjavam adroho nābhimānaś ca hrīs titikṣā damaḥ śamaḥ
english: in whom dwell kindness and truth, harmlessness, austerity, uprightness, freedom from malice and from pride, modesty, forbearance, self-restraint, and calm;

sanskrit: hrīmān satyadhṛtir dānto bhūtānām avihiṃsakaḥ akāmadveṣasaṃyuktas tribhiḥ śuklaiḥ samanvitaḥ
english: the man of modesty, firm in truth, self-controlled, who does no harm to living beings, free from desire and hatred, endowed with the three pure qualities;

sanskrit: ahiṃsako jñānatṛptaḥ sa brahmāsanam arhati ete mahartvijas tāta sarve mānyā yathātatham
english: harmless and satisfied in knowledge — he is worthy of the seat of brahman. These are the great officiating priests, my son, all to be honored according to their worth.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yad idaṃ vedavacanaṃ dakṣiṇāsu vidhīyate idaṃ deyam idaṃ deyaṃ na kva cid vyavatiṣṭhate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: This word of the Veda that is laid down concerning sacrificial fees — "this is to be given, this is to be given" — nowhere comes to a fixed limit.

sanskrit: nedaṃ prati dhanaṃ śāstram āpaddharmam aśāstrataḥ ājñā śāstrasya ghoreyaṃ na śaktiṃ samavekṣate
english: This teaching takes no account of one's wealth, nor of the dharma of distress, which lies outside the rule; this dread command of the scripture regards not a man's capacity.

sanskrit: śraddhām ārabhya yaṣṭavyam ity eṣā vaidikī śrutiḥ mithyopetasya yajñasya kim u śraddhā kariṣyati
english: "One should sacrifice beginning with faith" — such is the Vedic revelation; but for a sacrifice tainted with falsehood, what then will faith accomplish?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca na vedānāṃ paribhavān na śāṭhyena na māyayā kaś cin mahad avāpnoti mā te bhūd buddhir īdṛśī
english: Bhīṣma said: Not by contempt of the Vedas, not by guile, not by deceit does anyone attain to greatness; let no such notion be yours.

sanskrit: yajñāṅgaṃ dakṣiṇās tāta vedānāṃ paribṛṃhaṇam na mantrā dakṣiṇāhīnās tārayanti kathaṃ cana
english: The fees, my son, are a limb of the sacrifice, the strengthening of the Vedas; mantras bereft of fees can in no way carry one across.

sanskrit: śaktis tu pūrṇapātreṇa saṃmitānavamā bhavet avaśyaṃ tāta yaṣṭavyaṃ tribhir varṇair yathāvidhi
english: One's capacity, measured by a brimming vessel, becomes not the least defective; for surely, my son, by the three orders the sacrifice must be performed as prescribed.

sanskrit: somo rājā brāhmaṇānām ity eṣā vaidikī śrutiḥ taṃ ca vikretum icchanti na vṛthā vṛttir iṣyate tena krītena dharmeṇa tato yajñaḥ pratāyate
english: "Soma is the king of the Brāhmaṇas" — such is the Vedic revelation; and though they wish to sell him, no worthless livelihood is sanctioned. When he has been duly purchased according to dharma, the sacrifice is thereupon set in motion.
